question: The normal respiratory rate of a healthy newborn is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 40 to 60 breaths per minute

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A newborn breathes 40 to 60 times a minute because of a high metabolic rate and small lungs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 10 to 20 breaths per minute: Ten to twenty is well below the newborn range

C — 70 to 90 breaths per minute: Above 60 per minute indicates respiratory distress

D — 20 to 30 breaths per minute: Twenty to thirty per minute is normal for an older child

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Count the respirations for a full minute because newborn breathing is irregular

question: The maximum possible APGAR score of a newborn is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 10

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Five components are each scored from 0 to 2, giving a maximum total of 10

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20: Twenty cannot be reached on any component scoring

C — 15: Fifteen is more than the scale allows

D — 5: Five is the number of components, not the maximum score

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Scores of 7 to 10 are considered normal at one minute

question: The Moro reflex of a newborn is elicited by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a sudden change of position or a loud noise, which makes the arms extend and then embrace

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Moro or startle reflex causes symmetrical abduction of the arms followed by an embrace movement

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — touching the cheek, which makes the head turn towards the stimulus: Turning the head towards a cheek stimulus is the rooting reflex

B — stroking the sole of the foot, which makes the toes fan out: Fanning of the toes is the Babinski reflex

C — placing a finger in the palm, which makes the baby grip it: Gripping a finger is the palmar grasp reflex

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: An absent or asymmetrical Moro reflex suggests neurological or brachial plexus injury
option_1: touching the cheek, which makes the head turn towards the stimulus
option_2: stroking the sole of the foot, which makes the toes fan out
option_3: placing a finger in the palm, which makes the baby grip it
option_4: a sudden change of position or a loud noise, which makes the arms extend and then embrace

question: Kangaroo mother care should be started in a low-birth-weight baby:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. as soon as the baby is stable and breathing well without distress

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Once the baby is stable, breathing well and able to feed, skin-to-skin care can begin, often within hours of birth

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only when the baby can be bottle fed: KMC is suitable even for babies on tube feeds and is unrelated to bottle feeding

B — only after discharge from hospital: KMC is begun in hospital and continued at home

C — only after the baby reaches 3 kg: Waiting for a 3 kg weight denies the baby the benefits of KMC

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: KMC provides warmth, breastfeeding support and bonding in one simple method
option_1: only when the baby can be bottle fed
option_4: as soon as the baby is stable and breathing well without distress

question: In kangaroo mother care the baby is positioned:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. upright and skin-to-skin between the mother's breasts, with the head turned to one side

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The baby lies upright, skin-to-skin on the mother's chest, head turned to the side and slightly extended to keep the airway open

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — lying supine in a cot beside the mother: A cot does not provide the warmth and stability of skin-to-skin contact

B — prone on the mother's abdomen after a feed only: KMC is continuous, not limited to the period after a feed

D — wrapped in a blanket on the mother's lap: A blanket between mother and baby prevents direct skin contact

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: A firm binder or cloth secures the baby to the mother's chest so that she can move about
option_1: lying supine in a cot beside the mother
option_2: prone on the mother's abdomen after a feed only
option_3: upright and skin-to-skin between the mother's breasts, with the head turned to one side
option_4: wrapped in a blanket on the mother's lap

question: A premature baby on kangaroo mother care has a temperature of 36.2 °C. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. cover the baby's head with a cap, wrap both mother and baby and recheck the temperature

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Additional covering and a cap reduce heat loss, so the temperature is rechecked after these measures

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give the baby cold water to drink: Cold water lowers the core temperature further and is dangerous

B — switch on a fan over the baby: A fan increases convective heat loss

C — remove the baby from the mother and bathe him: Bathing a cold preterm baby causes further heat loss

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: A preterm baby loses heat rapidly because of a large surface area and little fat
option_1: give the baby cold water to drink
option_2: switch on a fan over the baby
option_3: remove the baby from the mother and bathe him
option_4: cover the baby's head with a cap, wrap both mother and baby and recheck the temperature

question: Jaundice appearing within the first twenty-four hours of a newborn's life is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. always pathological and needs urgent investigation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Jaundice in the first day of life is never physiological and suggests haemolysis, infection or another serious cause

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — not important if the baby is feeding: A feeding baby can still have dangerous jaundice

B — a normal finding: Physiological jaundice appears only after the first day

D — due to breast milk alone: Breast milk jaundice occurs later and is a diagnosis of exclusion

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Measure the serum bilirubin and the blood group of mother and baby without delay
option_1: not important if the baby is feeding

question: During phototherapy for a jaundiced newborn, the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. keep the baby naked except for a nappy with eyes protected, turn frequently and maintain hydration

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Maximum skin exposure with protected eyes, frequent turning and adequate fluids make phototherapy effective and safe

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — stop breastfeeding for the duration of phototherapy: Breastfeeding should continue and even be increased during phototherapy

B — apply oil to the skin before starting the light: Oil on the skin can cause burns under the lamp

D — cover the baby fully with a blanket under the light: Covering the skin prevents the light from breaking down bilirubin

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The light should be as close as the manufacturer permits, with the baby's temperature monitored
option_1: stop breastfeeding for the duration of phototherapy
option_2: apply oil to the skin before starting the light
option_3: keep the baby naked except for a nappy with eyes protected, turn frequently and maintain hydration
option_4: cover the baby fully with a blanket under the light

question: A severely jaundiced newborn develops a high-pitched cry, arching of the back and opisthotonus. These signs indicate:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. kernicterus from bilirubin deposition in the brain

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A high-pitched cry and arching of the back with opisthotonus indicate bilirubin encephalopathy, or kernicterus

🔍 Key Clues: newborn

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — hypoglycaemia: Hypoglycaemia causes jitteriness and sweating, not opisthotonus

B — normal newborn behaviour: These are not normal newborn behaviours

D — a minor feeding problem: A feeding problem does not produce arching of the back

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Kernicterus can leave permanent deafness, cerebral palsy and intellectual disability
option_3: kernicterus from bilirubin deposition in the brain

question: Respiratory distress syndrome in a preterm newborn is caused by deficiency of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. surfactant in the alveoli

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Without surfactant the alveoli collapse at the end of every breath, causing progressive respiratory distress

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — oxygen in the blood: Lack of oxygen is the result, not the cause, of the syndrome

B — vitamin K: Vitamin K deficiency causes bleeding, not respiratory distress

C — plasma proteins: Plasma proteins have no role in alveolar stability

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The risk falls as gestation advances because surfactant production increases after 34 weeks

question: A preterm baby at two hours of age has grunting, nasal flaring and intercostal retractions. The nurse should recognise that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the baby has respiratory distress and needs oxygen and urgent assessment

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Grunting, flaring and retractions are the classic signs of respiratory distress and call for oxygen and immediate medical assessment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — these are normal findings in a preterm baby: These signs are never normal, even in a preterm baby

B — the baby is simply hungry: Hunger does not cause grunting or retractions

C — the baby needs an early bath: Bathing a distressed baby is contraindicated

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Record the respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and the severity of retractions
option_1: these are normal findings in a preterm baby
option_4: the baby has respiratory distress and needs oxygen and urgent assessment

question: Surfactant replacement therapy in a newborn with respiratory distress syndrome is given by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. instilling the drug directly into the trachea through the endotracheal tube

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Surfactant is instilled directly into the trachea so that it reaches the alveoli

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a nebuliser mask: A nebuliser does not deliver an adequate dose to the alveoli

B — an intramuscular injection: An intramuscular injection would not reach the lungs

D — an intravenous infusion: Intravenous administration is not effective for surfactant

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Watch for bradycardia and desaturation while the drug is being instilled
option_3: instilling the drug directly into the trachea through the endotracheal tube

question: Which antenatal measure most reduces the risk of respiratory distress syndrome in a preterm baby?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. giving corticosteroids to the mother before preterm delivery

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Antenatal corticosteroids accelerate fetal surfactant production and reduce both the incidence and severity of RDS

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — restricting the mother's fluids: Fluid restriction has no effect on surfactant production

B — giving antibiotics to the mother: Antibiotics treat infection but do not mature the lungs

D — performing an early caesarean section: Early delivery without steroids increases the risk of RDS

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Steroids are most effective when given at least 24 hours before delivery
option_3: giving corticosteroids to the mother before preterm delivery

question: The dose of paracetamol for a child is usually calculated according to the child's:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. body weight

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Paracetamol for children is prescribed per kilogram of body weight, usually 10 to 15 mg/kg per dose

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — body surface area of an adult: Adult surface area is irrelevant to a child's dose

B — height: Height is not used for paracetamol dosing

D — age in months only: Age alone is unreliable because children of the same age vary greatly in size

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Always weigh the child and check the maximum daily dose

question: The antibiotics commonly started for a newborn with suspected sepsis are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. ampicillin and gentamicin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Ampicillin with gentamicin covers the common organisms causing early-onset neonatal sepsis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — metronidazole alone: Metronidazole alone covers only anaerobes

B — rifampicin and isoniazid: Rifampicin and isoniazid are antitubercular drugs

C — ciprofloxacin alone: Ciprofloxacin alone is not the first-line choice in neonates

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Check renal function and hearing when gentamicin is given for more than a few days

question: The dose of vitamin K given intramuscularly to a term newborn is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 1 mg

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A single intramuscular dose of 1 mg of vitamin K is given to a term newborn, and 0.5 mg to a preterm baby

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 0.1 mg: A tenth of a milligram is too small to prevent bleeding

B — 5 mg: Five milligrams is higher than the standard dose

D — 10 mg: Ten milligrams far exceeds the recommended dose

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The injection is given into the anterolateral thigh within the first hour of life

question: A preterm baby has a blood glucose of 30 mg/dL and remains jittery after a feed. The nurse should prepare to give:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 10% dextrose intravenously as prescribed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A symptomatic baby with a glucose of 30 mg/dL needs intravenous 10% dextrose to correct the level quickly

🔍 Key Clues: 30 mg/dL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — nothing at all until the next feed: Delay risks seizures and brain injury

B — a strong sugar solution orally and no further action: Oral sugar helps in mild cases but is not enough for a symptomatic preterm baby

C — plain water by mouth: Plain water does not raise the blood glucose

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Recheck the glucose fifteen to thirty minutes after starting treatment
option_1: nothing at all until the next feed
option_2: a strong sugar solution orally and no further action

question: Which drug is used to close a haemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus in a preterm baby?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. indomethacin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Indomethacin, a prostaglandin synthetase inhibitor, closes the ductus in most preterm babies

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — frusemide: Frusemide is a diuretic and may even keep the ductus open

C — digoxin: Digoxin is used in heart failure but does not close the ductus

D — adrenaline: Adrenaline raises the blood pressure but does not close the duct

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Watch the urine output and renal function during indomethacin therapy

question: Oral rehydration solution is given to a child with acute diarrhoea because it:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. replaces water and electrolytes lost in the stools

🧠 Clinical Rationale: ORS contains sodium, potassium, chloride, citrate and glucose in the right proportions to replace losses

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — kills the infecting organism: ORS has no antimicrobial action

C — prevents all future attacks of diarrhoea: It does not confer protection against future episodes

D — stops the diarrhoea immediately: ORS does not stop the diarrhoea; it prevents dehydration while the illness runs its course

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Zinc given with ORS shortens the duration of diarrhoea
option_2: replaces water and electrolytes lost in the stools

question: Which drug is the specific antidote for iron poisoning in a child?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. desferrioxamine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Desferrioxamine chelates iron and promotes its excretion in iron poisoning

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — naloxone: Naloxone reverses opioids

B — protamine sulphate: Protamine sulphate reverses heparin

C — calcium gluconate: Calcium gluconate is used in hyperkalaemia and magnesium toxicity

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Iron tablets are a common cause of serious poisoning because they look like sweets

question: Zinc supplementation in a child with diarrhoea:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. reduces the duration and severity of the illness

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Zinc given for 14 days reduces the duration and severity of diarrhoea and prevents recurrence

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — stops growth: Zinc promotes growth rather than impairing it

B — causes constipation: Constipation is not an expected effect

C — has no effect on diarrhoea: Numerous trials have shown a definite benefit

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Zinc is given for 14 days to every child with diarrhoea under the national programme
option_4: reduces the duration and severity of the illness

question: Which drug is usually the first choice for controlling convulsions in a neonate?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. phenobarbitone

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Phenobarbitone is the drug of choice for neonatal seizures because it is effective and well studied in this age group

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — sodium valproate: Sodium valproate is avoided in the newborn

C — lamotrigine: Lamotrigine is not used for neonatal seizures

D — carbamazepine: Carbamazepine is used in older children and adults

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

question: For a child with some dehydration, the volume of oral rehydration solution given over four hours (Plan B) is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 75 mL per kilogram of body weight

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Plan B gives about 75 mL per kg of ORS over four hours, with continued breastfeeding

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 500 mL in total for any weight: A fixed volume ignores the child's weight

C — 200 mL per kilogram: Two hundred mL per kg risks fluid overload

D — 10 mL per kilogram: Ten mL per kg is far too little to correct dehydration

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Reassess the child after four hours and change the plan if needed
option_1: 75 mL per kilogram of body weight
option_2: 500 mL in total for any weight

question: The first-line drug for anaphylaxis in a child is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. adrenaline given intramuscularly into the anterolateral thigh

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Intramuscular adrenaline reverses bronchospasm, hypotension and swelling and must be given at once

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a bronchodilator by nebuliser alone: A nebulised bronchodilator does not correct hypotension

C — an antihistamine by mouth: Oral antihistamines act too slowly to save a life

💎 PNC Pearl: Repeat the adrenaline after five to fifteen minutes if there is no improvement
option_1: adrenaline given intramuscularly into the anterolateral thigh

question: The normal heart rate of a healthy newborn is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 120 to 160 per minute

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A newborn's heart normally beats between 120 and 160 times a minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 40 to 60 per minute: Forty to sixty is far too slow for a newborn

B — 180 to 220 per minute: Above 160 is tachycardia in a newborn

D — 60 to 80 per minute: Sixty to eighty is an adult rate

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

question: The total number of deciduous (milk) teeth in a child is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 20

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A child has twenty deciduous teeth, which are gradually replaced by permanent teeth

A — 32: Thirty-two is the number of permanent teeth in an adult

B — 16: Sixteen would leave part of each jaw without teeth

D — 24: Twenty-four is neither the milk nor the permanent number

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

question: The ductus arteriosus in a newborn normally closes:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. within the first few days after birth

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Functional closure of the ductus arteriosus occurs within hours to days of birth, and anatomical closure takes a few weeks

question: Which fetal shunt allows blood to pass directly from the right atrium to the left atrium?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the foramen ovale

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The foramen ovale is an opening in the atrial septum that lets oxygenated blood bypass the lungs

question: The normal blood pressure of a healthy newborn is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 70/50 mm Hg

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: Moulding of the fetal head during delivery is possible because:
solution:

B — the skull contains no bone at all: Most of the skull is bone at birth

C — the brain is soft and can be compressed: The brain cannot be compressed without injury

option_2: the skull contains no bone at all

question: A newborn has more bones than an adult because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. many bones are still separate and fuse later in life

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A newborn has about 300 separate bony and cartilaginous elements that gradually fuse into the 206 bones of the adult

option_1: the number of bones does not change with age

option_3: many bones are still separate and fuse later in life

question: The type of haemoglobin that predominates in the fetus and newborn is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. fetal haemoglobin (HbF)

question: The normal respiratory rate of a child aged one to five years is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 20 to 30 breaths per minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 60 to 80 breaths per minute: Above sixty in this age group indicates severe distress

C — 40 to 60 breaths per minute: Forty to sixty is the newborn rate

D — 12 to 16 breaths per minute: Twelve to sixteen is an adult rate

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Count respirations when the child is calm and not crying

question: The neonatal period is defined as the first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. twenty-eight days of life

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The neonatal period is the first 28 days of life and is the time of highest mortality

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — one year of life: The first year is the infancy period

B — three months of life: The first three months is part of infancy

C — seven days of life: The first week is only the early neonatal period

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Most neonatal deaths occur in the first week, so early home visits matter

question: In the nursing process, the step in which the nurse compares the child's progress with the goals that were planned is:
solution:

question: A two-year-old admitted with severe malnutrition has an indwelling nasogastric tube for feeds. Before each feed the nurse should first:
solution:

question: Which oxygen delivery device gives the most constant and predictable oxygen concentration to a small infant?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. head box (oxyhood)

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A head box encloses the head in a known volume of gas, so the inspired oxygen concentration stays constant and can be measured

question: Consent for an elective operation on a child of twelve years must be obtained from:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the child's parent or legal guardian

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A child of twelve is a minor, so the parent or legally appointed guardian gives the valid consent

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — any adult relative who happens to be present: Only a parent or legally appointed guardian can consent, and not any relative who is present

B — the child alone: A minor cannot give legal consent for surgery in India

D — the ward sister on duty: The ward sister has no legal authority to consent on behalf of a patient

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: It is good practice to take the child's assent as well, so that preparation and anaesthesia go smoothly
option_1: any adult relative who happens to be present

question: Which Indian state produces the largest share of the country's salt?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Gujarat

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Gujarat, with its long Arabian Sea coast and favourable evaporation conditions, produces about three quarters of India's salt

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Odisha: Odisha produces only a very small quantity of salt

C — Rajasthan: Rajasthan has some inland salt lakes but only a small share of production

D — Tamil Nadu: Tamil Nadu produces salt but far less than Gujarat

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Iodised salt is the mainstay of goitre prevention, so nurses must know which salt is properly iodised

question: The Brahmaputra river is known in Tibet by which name?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Yarlung Tsangpo

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo and becomes the Brahmaputra after entering India

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Salween: The Salween is a separate river flowing through China and Myanmar

C — Mekong: The Mekong flows through south-east Asia and is not connected to the Brahmaputra

D — Irrawaddy: The Irrawaddy is the main river of Myanmar

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Floods along the Brahmaputra valley displace large populations, so relief planning and safe water supply are regular nursing duties there

question: The minimum age required to become a member of the Rajya Sabha is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 30 years

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Article 80 of the Constitution fixes thirty years as the minimum age for membership of the Rajya Sabha

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 35 years: Thirty-five years is the minimum age to become President of India

B — 21 years: Twenty-one years is the minimum voting age, not the age for the Rajya Sabha

C — 25 years: Twenty-five years is the minimum age for the Lok Sabha

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Health legislation for nurses passes through these houses, so knowing their composition helps in professional advocacy

question: In India, the repo rate is decided by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Bank of India

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A six-member Monetary Policy Committee set up under the Reserve Bank of India Act decides the repo rate

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the Planning Commission: The Planning Commission has been replaced by NITI Aayog and never set interest rates

C — the State Bank of India: The State Bank of India is a commercial bank and does not set the repo rate

D — the Ministry of Finance: The Ministry of Finance frames fiscal policy, not monetary policy

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Interest rates and inflation affect the real value of a nurse's salary and the cost of health care
option_1: the Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Bank of India

question: The World Health Organization came into being in which year?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1948

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The World Health Organization was established on 7 April 1948, and that date is now observed as World Health Day

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1945: 1945 was the year the United Nations was founded, before the health agency existed

C — 1946: 1946 was the year the constitution of the organization was adopted, before it came into force

D — 1950: By 1950 the organization was already functioning and running its first programmes

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: WHO standards, such as the ORS formula and immunization schedules, are the basis of Indian nursing practice

question: The Battle of Plassey was fought in which year?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 1757

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah at Plassey in 1757, which established British political power in Bengal

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 1707: 1707 was the year of Aurangzeb's death

C — 1764: 1764 was the year of the Battle of Buxar, fought later than Plassey

D — 1857: 1857 was the year of the First War of Indian Independence

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Public health institutions in India, including nursing schools, grew out of this colonial administrative system

question: The Duncan Passage lies between:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. South Andaman and Little Andaman

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Duncan Passage is the narrow strait separating South Andaman from Little Andaman

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — India and Sri Lanka: India and Sri Lanka are separated by the Palk Strait

C — North Andaman and Middle Andaman: North and Middle Andaman are separated by the Austin Strait

D — Great Nicobar and Sumatra: Great Nicobar and Sumatra lie across the Six Degree Channel and the Andaman Sea

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: These islands depend on ships and aircraft for medical evacuation, which shapes their nursing contingency plans

question: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of human blood groups was awarded to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Karl Landsteiner

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Karl Landsteiner won the 1930 Nobel Prize for describing the ABO blood group system

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Alexander Fleming: Alexander Fleming shared the Nobel Prize for the discovery of penicillin

B — Louis Pasteur: Louis Pasteur never received the Nobel Prize

C — Robert Koch: Robert Koch won it for work on tuberculosis

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The ABO system is the basis of safe blood transfusion and of compatibility testing in every ward

question: The SI unit of pressure is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. pascal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: One pascal is a force of one newton acting on an area of one square metre

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — joule: The joule is the SI unit of energy and work

C — newton: The newton is the SI unit of force

D — watt: The watt is the SI unit of power

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Blood pressure is recorded in millimetres of mercury, but the underlying quantity is pressure and its SI unit is the pascal

question: In a lever of the first order, the fulcrum lies:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. between the load and the effort

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A first-order lever, such as a see-saw or a pair of scissors, has the fulcrum between the load and the effort

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — outside the lever: The fulcrum is always a point on the lever itself

C — at one end with the load in the middle: A load between the fulcrum and the effort makes a second-order lever, like a wheelbarrow

D — at one end with the effort in the middle: An effort between the fulcrum and the load makes a third-order lever, like a pair of forceps

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Knowing lever classes helps the nurse use forceps and lifting aids without straining the back
option_3: at one end with the load in the middle
option_4: at one end with the effort in the middle

question: Heavy water is chemically:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. deuterium oxide

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Heavy water is deuterium oxide, in which the hydrogen atoms are replaced by deuterium

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — hydrogen peroxide: Hydrogen peroxide is a different compound used as a disinfectant

B — distilled water: Distilled water is ordinary water freed of dissolved salts

D — tritium oxide: Tritium oxide is sometimes called super-heavy water

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Heavy water is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors, which is why reactors need careful radiation safety planning

question: Which colour of visible light has the shortest wavelength?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. violet

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Violet lies at the short-wavelength end of the visible spectrum, with a wavelength of about 400 nanometres

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — green: Green lies in the middle of the spectrum

C — red: Red has the longest wavelength of visible light

D — yellow: Yellow has a longer wavelength than green

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Ultraviolet light beyond violet causes skin damage, which is why phototherapy units and sun exposure are both used cautiously

question: The frequency range normally audible to a healthy young human ear is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The human ear responds to frequencies from about 20 to 20,000 cycles per second

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20,000 Hz to 200,000 Hz: Frequencies above 20,000 Hz are ultrasound and cannot be heard

C — 200 Hz to 2,000 Hz: 200 to 2,000 Hz is only the middle part of the audible range

D — 2 Hz to 200 Hz: Frequencies of 2 to 200 Hz are almost all below the audible range

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Hearing screening in newborns and school children tests exactly this range, and noise above 85 decibels damages it

question: Which material is the best conductor of electricity?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. silver

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Silver has the lowest electrical resistivity of all metals

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — aluminium: Aluminium conducts well but less efficiently than copper

B — iron: Iron has a comparatively high resistivity among metals

C — copper: Copper is an excellent conductor but slightly less so than silver

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Conductive gels, saline and wet skin lower electrical resistance, which is why defibrillator safety rules matter

question: Short-sightedness, or myopia, is corrected by using:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a concave lens

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina, so a concave lens diverges the light and pushes the focus back on to the retina

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a bifocal lens: A bifocal lens helps presbyopia, in which near vision is lost with age

B — a convex lens: A convex lens converges light and is used for long-sightedness

D — a cylindrical lens: A cylindrical lens corrects astigmatism rather than simple myopia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: School vision screening identifies myopia early, and uncorrected refractive error is a common cause of poor school performance

question: Which greenhouse gas is released in the largest quantity by human activity?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. carbon dioxide

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels makes up the greatest share of human greenhouse gas emissions

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — nitrous oxide: Nitrous oxide is a minor contributor in terms of total mass

C — methane: Methane is more potent per molecule but is released in far smaller quantity

D — ozone: Ozone is a pollutant and a greenhouse gas but is not emitted in bulk by human activity

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Heat waves and vector-borne disease patterns respond to climate, which is why the health sector tracks emissions

question: If 25 percent of a number is 60, then the number is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 240

🧠 Method: If one quarter of the number is 60, the number is 60 multiplied by 4, which is 240

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 150: 150 would give 37.5 as one quarter, not 60

C — 320: 320 gives 80 as one quarter

D — 180: 180 gives 45 as one quarter

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Nurses use percentages to work out concentration of solutions and to read laboratory reports accurately

question: The average of 12, 18, 24 and 26 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 20

🧠 Method: The sum is 80 and dividing by 4 gives an average of 20

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 22: 22 is higher than the true average of these four numbers

B — 18: 18 is the second number and not the average

D — 24: 24 is the third number and not the average

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Averages are used to summarise ward statistics such as average length of stay and average temperature readings

question: The ratio of 45 minutes to 2 hours is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 3 : 8

🧠 Method: Two hours is 120 minutes, so the ratio is 45 to 120, which reduces to 3 to 8

⚡ Fast Approach: Add the parts to get the total number of parts, then find the value of one part.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 9 : 4: 9 to 4 results from inverting the correct ratio

C — 4 : 9: 4 to 9 is also the inverted form of the correct answer

D — 45 : 2: The two quantities must first be expressed in the same unit before the ratio is taken

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Ratios are needed to dilute disinfectants and to calculate drug concentrations correctly

question: The simple interest on 5,000 rupees at 8 percent per annum for 3 years is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1,200 rupees

🧠 Method: Simple interest is 5000 multiplied by 8 multiplied by 3 and divided by 100, which gives 1,200 rupees

⚡ Fast Approach: SI = P x R x T / 100. Keep T in years - convert months to a fraction.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1,400 rupees: 1,400 rupees would need a higher rate or a longer period

C — 400 rupees: 400 rupees is the interest for a single year only

D — 1,000 rupees: 1,000 rupees does not correspond to any whole number of years at this rate

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Understanding interest helps nurses judge loan and insurance schemes offered to them

question: An article bought for 400 rupees is sold for 500 rupees. The profit percent is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 25 percent

🧠 Method: The profit is 100 rupees, and 100 as a percentage of the cost price of 400 is 25 percent

⚡ Fast Approach: Profit percent is always on the cost price, loss percent also on the cost price.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 10 percent: 10 percent is far below the actual profit

B — 20 percent: 20 percent is the profit calculated on the selling price, which is not the correct base

C — 30 percent: 30 percent is higher than the actual profit

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Profit percentage is always worked out on the cost price, a distinction that matters in hospital supply costing

question: A can complete a task in 12 days and B can complete the same task in 18 days. Working together, they will finish it in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 7.2 days

🧠 Method: In one day they finish one-twelfth plus one-eighteenth, which is five thirty-sixths, so the whole task takes 36 divided by 5, that is 7.2 days

⚡ Fast Approach: Combine rates as 1/A + 1/B, then invert to get the number of days.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 6 days: 6 days would need a combined rate faster than the two rates actually allow

C — 9 days: 9 days is longer than the true combined time

D — 15 days: 15 days is the arithmetic mean of 12 and 18 and ignores that they work at the same time

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The same rate logic is used to plan how many nurses are needed to complete a set of procedures in a shift

question: The population of a town first increases by 10 percent and then decreases by 10 percent. The net change in population is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a decrease of 1 percent

🧠 Method: On a base of 100 the population rises to 110 and then falls by 10 percent of 110, which is 11, leaving 99, a net fall of 1 percent

⚡ Fast Approach: Take a base of 100, apply the changes one after another, and compare the final figure with the base.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a decrease of 10 percent: A fall of 10 percent would need the second change to act on the original population

B — no change: The two changes are calculated on different bases, so the population does not return to its original value

D — an increase of 1 percent: The final figure is below the original and not above it

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Successive percentages in health coverage reports must be worked out on the current base, not the original one

question: Complete the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 42

🧠 Method: The differences are 4, 6, 8 and 10, so the next difference is 12 and 30 plus 12 gives 42

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 36: 36 would need a difference of only 6

B — 44: 44 would need a difference of 14

D — 40: 40 would need the last difference to be 10 rather than 12

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Series reasoning trains the pattern recognition used when reading trend graphs and monitoring charts

question: If TEACHER is coded as VGCEJGT, then STUDENT will be coded as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. UVWFGPV

🧠 Method: Each letter moves two places forward in the alphabet, so S becomes U, T becomes V, U becomes W, D becomes F, E becomes G, N becomes P and T becomes V

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — UVVFGPV: The third letter should be W and not V

B — UVWFGVP: The last three letters are in the wrong order

C — UWVFGPV: The third letter W has been placed second

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Careful step-by-step decoding mirrors the accuracy needed when transcribing drug orders

question: Pointing to a photograph, a man says, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the girl related to him?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. sister

🧠 Method: The grandfather's only son must be the man's own father, so the girl is his sister

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the family tree and mark the given relations before answering.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — daughter: His daughter would be described through himself and not through his grandfather

B — niece: A niece would be the child of his brother or sister, not of his father

D — cousin: A cousin would be the child of an uncle or aunt, but there is no uncle here

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Genograms in family nursing use exactly this kind of relationship reasoning to map inherited risk

question: A man walks 5 km towards the north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right again and walks 5 km. How far is he from the starting point?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 3 km

🧠 Method: The two north-south legs of 5 km cancel each other, leaving only the 3 km walked towards the east

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw a small diagram - each turn changes the direction by a fixed angle.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 13 km: 13 km is simply the total distance walked

C — 8 km: 8 km adds distances that lie in opposite directions

D — 5 km: 5 km is the length of each north-south leg and not the net displacement

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: The same reasoning underlies reading a site plan when locating a ward or an emergency exit

question: Which of the following does not belong to the group?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 9

🧠 Method: 9 is the only number in the group that is not a prime, since it is divisible by 3

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 7: 7 is a prime number and fits the group

B — 3: 3 is a prime number and fits the group

C — 5: 5 is a prime number and fits the group

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Spotting the odd item out is a form of the critical thinking used to detect an anomalous observation on a chart

question: All nurses are graduates. Some graduates are teachers. Which conclusion definitely follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Some graduates are nurses

🧠 Method: If every nurse is a graduate, then at least some graduates must be nurses, so this conclusion follows directly

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — All graduates are nurses: Only some graduates are nurses, not all of them

B — No nurse is a teacher: The statements do not rule out a nurse who is also a teacher

C — All teachers are nurses: Nothing in the statements says that all teachers are nurses

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Distinguishing what follows from what merely seems likely is central to drawing sound clinical inferences

question: In the English alphabet, which letter lies exactly midway between J and R?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. N

🧠 Method: J is the tenth letter and R is the eighteenth, so the middle position is the fourteenth, which is N

⚡ Fast Approach: Number the letters A=1 to Z=26 and work with numbers instead of letters.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — O: O is the fifteenth letter and lies too far to the right

C — P: P is the sixteenth letter and is not the midpoint

D — M: M is the thirteenth letter and lies too far to the left

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Accurate counting along a sequence is the same skill used when tallying doses or counting respiration rates
